detail.jawCaution: Skip this one if you have jaw pain, clicking or a TMJ problem.
detail.handsCaution: Use clean hands and light pressure. Skip irritated skin, and don't press on an area treated with Botox or fillers recently.

chinLift.name: Chin Lift
chinLift.cue: Tilt your head back and push your lower lip over your top lip.
steps: Sit or stand with a straight back.
Tilt your head back until you look at the ceiling.
Push your lower lip up over your top lip and feel the front of your neck stretch.

cheekLift.name: Cheek Lift
cheekLift.cue: Smile wide with closed lips and lift your cheeks toward your eyes.
steps: Keep your lips closed.
Smile as wide as you can and push your cheeks up toward your eyes.
Hold, then relax your face completely.

fishFace.name: Fish Face
fishFace.cue: Suck your cheeks in and pucker your lips.
steps: Suck your cheeks in between your teeth.
Pucker your lips like a fish.
Hold, then release and relax.

browLift.name: Brow Lift
browLift.cue: Raise your eyebrows as high as you can.
steps: Look straight ahead with a relaxed face.
Lift your eyebrows as high as you can.
Hold, then lower them slowly.

wideEyes.name: Wide Eyes
wideEyes.cue: Open your eyes as wide as you can without lifting your eyebrows.
steps: Rest a fingertip lightly on each eyebrow if it helps you keep your forehead still.
Open your eyes as wide as you can, as if surprised, without lifting your eyebrows.
Hold and stare at one point, then relax your eyes.

pout.name: Pout
pout.cue: Push your lips forward into a long pout, like a kiss.
steps: Keep your teeth apart and your face relaxed.
Push your lips forward as far as is comfortable, as if blowing a kiss.
Hold, then relax your lips.

templeCircles.name: Temple Circles
templeCircles.cue: Slow, gentle circles on your temples.
steps: Place your fingertips on your temples, beside your eyes.
Make slow circles with light pressure while you breathe out slowly.
Rest your hands, then repeat.

forehead.name: Forehead
forehead.about: The frontalis raises your eyebrows. The corrugator, between the brows, draws them together when you frown.

temples.name: Temples
temples.about: The temporalis is a fan-shaped chewing muscle at the side of your head. It works with the masseter when you bite.

eyes.name: Eyes
eyes.about: The orbicularis oculi is the ring of muscle around each eye. It closes the lids and makes you squint. Small muscles in the upper lids lift them.

cheeks.name: Cheeks
cheeks.about: The zygomaticus muscles pull the corners of your mouth up when you smile. The buccinator lies deeper and holds your cheeks against your teeth.

lips.name: Lips
lips.about: The orbicularis oris is the ring of muscle around your mouth. It closes, presses and puckers your lips.

jaw.name: Jaw
jaw.about: The masseter is a strong chewing muscle at the back of your jaw. Go gently, and skip jaw exercises if your jaw hurts or clicks.

chin.name: Chin
chin.about: The mentalis wrinkles your chin and pushes up your lower lip. Under the chin, the floor of your mouth works with your tongue when you swallow or press it to the palate.

neck.name: Neck
neck.about: The platysma is a thin sheet of muscle at the front of your neck. Deeper muscles hold your head up, so posture matters here.
